takeaway: Hot local-factor Tuesday: sunny morning, then isolated afternoon storms — showers look more scattered than the wet weekend, but a strong cell can still dump hard nearby. Surf winds: northerly/offshore today through Wednesday (best night and morning glass); Thursday softens and Friday leans Pacific/onshore. Watch Tropical Wave #48 later this week for a wetter pulse. Distant East Pacific storms stay near Mexico and farther west. Prolonged multi-day rain remains watch-only.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Tue–Thu)
periods.pattern: Costa Rica’s weather service says high heat, weak winds, and moist sea breezes drive Tuesday: few clouds over Pacífico Norte this morning, then afternoon cloud-up with isolated showers and storms; nights mostly quieter with only scattered coastal rain possible. Inland heat is sharp (Nicoya around 35–36°C, Liberia near 37°C). Humidity stays high, but rains look more dispersed than the wave-soaked weekend. Ensemble averages keep Nicoya daily rain mostly light to moderate — typical rainy-season cells, not a stuck rain machine. Midweek still favors Caribbean easterlies across Nicaragua and Nicoya at times, while Thursday’s near-surface Papagayo winds ease toward west–northwest.
periods.implications: Best outdoor window is morning before isolated storms build. Plan for heat. For surf, prioritize early sessions today through Wednesday while the northerly/offshore signal holds; Thursday is less reliable as flow softens.
periods.confidence: High that Tuesday is a local-factor day (not a named wave day) and no nearby cyclone hits Costa Rica. Moderate on exact Nosara shower timing and how clean Wednesday mornings stay before Thursday’s softer winds.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Fri–Mon)
periods.pattern: The official weekly outlook flags Tropical Wave #48 approaching in the second half of the week, which could bump rain activity again after the more scattered midweek pattern. Longer official guidance still leans drier than normal for Pacífico Norte into early October, with weekly Pacífico Norte totals in a light-to-moderate rainy-season range and no extreme-rain event flagged. Ensemble averages show a wetter pulse around the weekend into early next week — more Pacific-side moisture near Nicoya on some means — but without a Costa Rica–centered rain machine. Near-surface marine winds trend west through Friday and stay soft or west-leaning into the weekend.
periods.implications: Keep late-day and weekend plans flexible for quick storms if Wave #48 verifies. Surf-wind quality is better early in the week (Tue–Wed offshore) than Friday–weekend if Pacific/west flow holds. Nicaragua all-day offshore earlier in the week is a good Nosara morning-quality signal, but it does not mean Nosara stays glassy all day.
periods.confidence: Moderate for a weekend wetter pulse tied to Wave #48 and the quieter-than-peak Pacífico Norte theme; low–moderate on exact timing of the wetter days and how firmly Friday–Saturday onshore winds verify.

periods.label: Days 8–15
periods.pattern: Costa Rica’s longer-range outlook keeps Pacífico Norte drier than normal from late September into mid-October, with the dry signal strengthening after about October 12. No official extreme-rain event is flagged for this week. Ensemble means still allow some moist days into early October, but the baseline is not a prolonged flood-season spell. Distant East Pacific activity remains focused near Mexico and farther west.
periods.implications: Treat any wet day as a short cell unless a new watch develops. Outdoor and surf planning can assume the quieter Pacífico Norte lean until guidance changes.
periods.confidence: Moderate for the quieter-than-peak theme; low for day-by-day detail past about a week.

gyreWatch.possibleTiming: No focused gyre window; residual humid instability early week, then a general chance of a wetter pulse mid/late week into the weekend if Tropical Wave #48 and Pacific moisture reconnect
gyreWatch.supporting: Atmosphere remains humid after the wet weekend. Official weekly outlook cites Tropical Wave #48 later this week as a possible rain bump. Broad moist Pacific flow remains nearby offshore. Some ensemble means show wetter days around the weekend into early next week. Distant East Pacific storms keep the far-Pacific moisture field active near Mexico.
gyreWatch.conflicting: No closed gyre sits over Costa Rica or Nicaragua on the main ensemble averages. Official Tuesday Pacífico Norte forecast is only isolated afternoon storms under local factors, with rains more dispersed than prior days. Midweek Caribbean easterlies argue against a stuck onshore rain machine. The longer official outlook leans drier for northern Pacific into October, with no extreme event flagged for this week. Named East Pacific systems track along or well off Mexico, not toward Costa Rica.

surfWinds.regime: Caribbean/N–NW offshore Tue–Wed → softer W–NW Thu → Pacific/W Fri–Sat
surfWinds.detail: Papagayo waters: northerly about 10 kt today — a real offshore signal for west-facing Nosara, not light/variable. Tonight through Wednesday holds northwest to north around 10 kt. Thursday turns west–northwest, then west Thursday night through Friday; Saturday looks light/variable at Papagayo with west elsewhere. Mid-level maps agree on easterlies across Nicaragua and Nicoya into midweek (often stronger over Nicaragua). That Nicaragua all-day offshore signal usually means good Nosara morning quality, but Nosara is not necessarily offshore all day — especially once Thursday–Friday lean Pacific/west. Do not read Papagayo light/variable as all-day glass.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Overnight and early morning today through Wednesday while N–NW holds. Thursday less reliable. Friday–weekend favor early checks only if any glass survives before west/onshore flow. No clean all-day offshore Friday–Saturday signal.
surfWinds.confidence: High on Tuesday–Wednesday N–NW offshore from the marine forecast. Moderate on how quickly Thursday softens and whether Friday–Saturday stay firmly Pacific/onshore.

whatChanged: Monday’s light/variable Papagayo call flipped to a cleaner northerly ~10 kt offshore today through Wednesday. Official weekly outlook now names Tropical Wave #48 for a possible mid/late-week rain bump. Monday afternoon storm notices (humid leftover after the wet weekend) are aging — Tuesday’s official Pacífico Norte call is isolated local-factor storms, more dispersed than prior days. Polo and Nolo are now hurricanes; Rachel remains a tropical storm south-southwest of Mexico — none threaten Costa Rica. Prolonged-rain watch stays watch-only.
practical: Best outdoors: Tuesday morning before isolated afternoon storms; expect strong inland heat. For surf, prioritize early glass today through Wednesday on the N–NW offshore; Thursday softens and Friday leans choppier. Watch the weekend if Wave #48 bumps rain. Prolonged multi-day rain is not the baseline. Latest official storm notices: Monday 28 Sep (11:00 a.m. and 5:50 p.m.) — strong afternoon storms under leftover humidity.
